caption: What if Betelgeuse exploded tonight? Betelgeuse is the red supergiant on Orion's shoulder, and in Indian astronomy it's linked to Ardra nakshatra. It's enormous: about 750 times the Sun's radius, so in our Sun's place it would swallow Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. When it goes supernova, astronomers expect it to shine about as bright as a half Moon, visible in daylight for roughly a year and at night for several years. Are we in danger? No. It's over 500 light-years away, far outside the danger zone. Don't stay up though: a 2020 study suggests the explosion is probably about 100,000 years away. The light you see tonight left it more than 500 years ago, before the Taj Mahal was built. Twist: much of the iron in your body was forged in exploding stars. Would YOU stay up to watch it? 👇
